captions.text: Hal was on shore leave and had two left feet,
so he asked me to sit instead of dance.
We sat at that little table half the night,
and he made me laugh so hard I spilled my soda.
I told my sister that night I'd marry him.

so he asked me to sit instead of dance.
We sat at that little table half the night,

I told my sister that night I'd marry him.

captions.text: I had three days of leave, so we didn't wait.
Evelyn carried white roses from her mother's garden.
My shipmates stood up for me in their dress blues on the courthouse steps.

lines.text: I had three days of leave, so we didn't wait.

captions.text: Hal makes it sound like a parade.
I held on to those roses the whole time, because they were Mother's.
His shipmates threw a whole sack of rice at us on the way down,
and Hal laughed so hard he nearly lost his cap.

captions.text: Every Sunday my mother made pancakes, and the whole kitchen smelled of butter and syrup.
I was allowed to pour the batter, badly.
My father pretended every lopsided one was the best he had ever eaten.

captions.text: It rained all morning, and I was sure the whole day was ruined.
Rick showed up with his good shoes soaked through and gave me his umbrella without a word.
By the time we came out of the chapel the sun was out.
And everyone was laughing at his socks.

lines.text: It rained all morning, and I was sure the whole day was ruined.
Rick showed up with his good shoes soaked through and gave me his umbrella without a word.
By the time we came out of the chapel the sun was out.
And everyone was laughing at his socks.

captions.text: Linda always says it rained, and Rick always says it didn't.
The one photo we have shows wet steps and a lot of umbrellas.
So I think she wins that one.

captions.text: Jenna was six weeks old the first time we drove to the coast in our little red van.
Mark waved at every car the whole way,
and Jenna slept through all of it.

captions.text: Mom lined all four of us up on the stone steps by the garden gate for the first day of school.
Daniel kept fixing his tie,
I wore my sailor dress,
and Ben, who wasn't even in school yet, refused to be left out.

captions.text: It was a blue bike with a bell, two sizes too big because I said he would grow into it.
I ran behind him holding the seat up and down the whole street.
When I finally let go he didn't notice for half a block.

captions.text: I just didn't want to stop, because stopping meant falling.
I noticed.
I rang the bell the whole way to the corner so he would know I was fine.

captions.text: I was thirteen and nobody expected me to win.
I held that trophy all the way home,
and Mom let me put it on the dinner table that night.

captions.text: Mark bought a blue station wagon that summer and decided we had to drive it to the Grand Canyon.
I sat in the back with a map I refused to read.
We got a flat tire outside a cherry stand.
We sat on a fruit crate and ate cherries while he fixed it.

lines.text: Mark bought a blue station wagon that summer and decided we had to drive it to the Grand Canyon.
I sat in the back with a map I refused to read.
We got a flat tire outside a cherry stand.
We sat on a fruit crate and ate cherries while he fixed it.

captions.text: Mark would not let anyone else drive that car.
When the tire went, he changed it in his good trousers.
Jenna ate so many cherries she was sick the rest of the way.

captions.text: I was so nervous I forgot Ben had the rings.
He walked up the aisle and pressed the box into my hand like it was nothing.
Mom and Dad sat on the front bench holding hands the whole time.
At the party Mom hugged me so hard my boutonniere fell off.

captions.text: Daniel looked exactly like he did on his first day of school, terrified and pretending not to be.
Ben saved the day with the rings.
When the confetti came down, Linda cried and I waved at everyone like a fool.

captions.text: We drove three states for the leaves and for Grandpa Hal,
who wanted every one of his great-grandkids on his lap at once.
Baby Nora fell asleep on him in the middle of the photo.

captions.text: For Mom's eightieth we put her in the big wicker loveseat with the brand-new twins.
She laughed so hard Theo started laughing too.
Lily and Nora wouldn't leave her side.

captions.text: Both grandmothers came and sat in the front row in matching hats, which was not planned.
Lily tripped on the stage stairs and turned it into a bow.
Carol clapped louder than anyone in the hall.
Outside she handed me that diploma, and I would not let go of her.

captions.text: My gown was too long and I caught the hem on the second step.
I figured if I bowed nobody would know.
Carsten knew, and he still brings it up every Thanksgiving.

captions.text: Linda sewed matching overalls for all six of us for the canoe trip,
so nobody could get lost.
We tipped the canoe anyway,
and Katie still says it was the best day of the summer.

captions.text: Mom swore she'd never get another cat,
then came home from the shelter with an orange kitten in her coat.
We named him Marmalade before we'd even closed the door.
